name: Apollo

summary.text: Apollo Global Management is a New York private-equity and asset-management firm. In October 2020 its board's Conflicts Committee, at the request of co-founder and chief executive Leon Black, retained Dechert LLP to review Black's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. The review, released January 25, 2021, found that Black paid Epstein $158 million between 2012 and 2017 for advice on trust and estate planning, tax, art, aircraft, yacht and philanthropy matters, that Apollo never did business with Epstein and Epstein never invested in Apollo funds, and that Dechert saw no evidence that Black or any Apollo employee was involved in Epstein's criminal activities. Black announced he would step down as CEO. The Senate Finance Committee has since investigated Black's tax planning and ties to Epstein, citing inconsistencies in the Dechert report.

facts.claim: At a regularly scheduled board meeting in October 2020 Leon Black asked Apollo's Conflicts Committee, made up of independent directors, to retain outside counsel for an independent review of his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein; the committee retained Dechert LLP, and Apollo released the findings on January 25, 2021.
facts.quote: At a regularly scheduled Board meeting in October 2020, Mr. Black requested the Conflicts Committee, comprised of independent directors, retain outside counsel to conduct an independent and thorough review.

facts.claim: The Dechert review found that Black's payments to Epstein totaled $158 million from 2012 to 2017, for work including advice on trust and estate planning, tax issues, artwork, Black's airplane and yacht, and philanthropy; it reported that Black stopped paying Epstein after a payment dispute and severed relations by October 2018.
facts.quote: Black was paid for work including advice on trust and estate planning, tax issues, issues relating to artwork, Blacks airplane, Blacks yacht, and philanthropy.

sources.title: Exhibit 99.1: Report of the Conflicts Committee / Dechert LLP review of Leon Black's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein
Apollo Global CEO Leon Black paid sex predator Jeffrey Epstein $158 million for financial advice after conviction

facts.claim: Dechert reported that it had seen no evidence that Black or any employee of his family office or Apollo was involved in any way with Epstein's criminal activities, while noting Black and others at Apollo knew of Epstein's 2008 conviction; Apollo stated it never did business with Epstein and that he never invested in Apollo-managed funds.
facts.quote: Dechert has seen no evidence that Black or any employee of the Family Office or Apollo was involved in any way with Epsteins criminal activities at any time.

sources.title: Exhibit 99.1: Report of the Conflicts Committee / Dechert LLP review of Leon Black's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein
Apollo Global Management Announces Conclusion and Release of Independent Review

facts.claim: The review attributed to Black and witnesses a belief that Epstein's advice conferred more than $1 billion and as much as $2 billion or more in value to Black, and concluded that public messaging from Black and Apollo had been substantially accurate but in two instances might warrant additional context or clarification.
facts.quote: Dechert concluded that the public messaging from Black and Apollo has been substantially accurate but, in two instances, may warrant additional context or clarification.

facts.claim: On January 25, 2021 CNN and CNBC reported that Leon Black would step down as Apollo's chief executive following the review, while remaining chairman.

facts.claim: Senate Finance Committee Chairman Ron Wyden wrote to Apollo CEO Marc Rowan in June 2022 and announced in July 2023 an ongoing investigation into Black's tax planning and financial ties with Epstein, which the committee said was prompted by inconsistencies in the Dechert report; the committee said Black had refused to answer questions or provide documents about how Epstein's compensation was set.
facts.quote: The committee said Black has refused to answer questions or provide any documents about how Epstein's compensation was set.

facts.claim: CNBC reported in June 2026 that Black told a House committee that Epstein had duped him out of more than $60 million in advisory fees by falsely claiming they were tax-deductible, and that what he believed to be $95 million of net fees over five years was actually $158 million; CNN reported in February 2026 that Apollo said there was nothing new in newly released Epstein documents.

openQuestions: Site claim that 'Apollo Global (Leon Black paid $158M for tax structures)' gained from Epstein: the $158 million was paid by Black personally, and the Dechert review states Apollo never did business with Epstein; the attribution to Apollo as a firm is not supported.

Site claim that Epstein's fees were for 'tax structures': the Dechert review lists trust and estate planning and tax issues among the services; the Senate Finance Committee disputes the value of that work.
The remaining site claims in the Epstein entry (Towers Financial, Carbyne, Acosta, Deutsche Bank, JPMorgan) do not concern Apollo and were not researched here.
Whether Black also left the Apollo chairmanship in 2021, and the date, was not covered by the sources returned.
